newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-INTER STAY ON COURSE FOR UEFA HAT-TRICK.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INTER STAY ON COURSE FOR UEFA HAT-TRICK.

text.p: Italy's Internazionale stayed on course for a 1990s UEFA Cup hat-trick on Tuesday by beating Anderlecht 3-2 on aggregate to reach the semifinals of this season's competition.
Spanish side Tenerife, with a dramatic late winner, French league leader Monaco and Germany's Schalke also moved through to the last four

Inter won Tuesday's home leg 2-1 while Monaco overwhelmed Newcastle 3-0 for a 4-0 aggregate. Tenerife, who lost 1-0 at home two weeks ago, turned things round in Denmark to beat Brondby 2-0, the winner coming in the last minute of extra-time. Schalke drew 1-1 in Valencia to complete a 3-1 aggregate victory. Inter lifted the trophy in 1991 and 1994 during a period when Italian teams totally dominated the competition.
Roy Hodgson's team may have thought they had done the difficult job by drawing 1-1 in Belgium but made hard work of the San Siro return leg.
Maurizio Ganz, who scored the first-leg goal, was on target again in the 12th minute but the Belgians levelled through Ghanaian Yaw Preko in the 33rd.
But Ganz settled it when he headed home his second goal of the night and fifth of the competition, after an hour and Inter held on.
"The thing that mattered was to win," said Hodgson, shrugging off criticism of Inter's below-par performance.

While Italy has won the cup six times in the last eight seasons, Spain last had a finalist in 1988 when Espanyol lost to Bayer Leverkusen and must go back two years further for a victory -- Real Madrid's thrashing of Cologne.
Their hopes now lie with Tenerife -- but they left it perilously late against Brondby.
Antonio Pinilla put Tenerife ahead and level on aggregate with a crisp shot after 21 minutes and the Spaniards had another effort cleared off the line and hit the bar in the second half.
Brondby's Bo Hansen saw his chip headed off the line by Julio Gento but it was Tenerife who looked the likely winners.
However, the tie looked destined for penalties until Antonio Mata Olivera curled in a low free-kick with virtually the last kick of the match.

"Our team showed in the two matches that they are superior in every aspect of the game," said Tenerife coach Jupp Heynckes, who missed the winning goal as he was busy planning who would take his team's penalties.
Monaco had looked impressive when chalking up a 1-0 win at Newcastle and continued where they left off on Tuesday.
Sylvian Legwinski got things going with a 30-metre drive after 41 minutes and Ali Benarbia lashed in the second in the 52nd.

Newcastle, missing injured first-choice strikers Alan Shearer and Les Ferdinand, never looked capable of turning it round and Benarbia completed the comfortable victory with a curling free-kick in the 67th minute.
"It will take a good side to beat them," Newcastle manager Kenny Dalglish said.
Schalke, who have never reached a European final, killed their match at Valencia as Youri Moulder put them ahead early, making it 3-0 on aggregate.
Antonio Poyatos pulled one back for the home side just before halftime but Schalke eased through to take their place in Friday's semifinal draw.
